\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পাহাড়} (pāhāṛ)}{পাহাড় (pāhāṛ)}]{\bn{পাহাড়} (pāhāṛ) — a mountain}

\label{lesson:BN-C66-pahar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a flower, then the Bengali for a leaf.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পাহাড়}}
\textbf{\bn{পাহাড়}} — \emph{pāhāṛ} — \textquotedblleft{}a mountain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পাহাড়}} (\emph{pāhāṛ}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*pāhāḍa}, \textquotedblleft{}rock, hill\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 8141). CDIAL thinks it probably connected with Sanskrit \emph{pāṣāṇa}, \textquotedblleft{}stone\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{pāhāṛ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a flower, then the Bengali for a leaf, then say \emph{pāhāṛ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নদী} (nôdi)}{নদী (nôdi)}]{\bn{নদী} (nôdi) — a river}

\label{lesson:BN-C66-nodi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a mountain, then the Bengali for a forest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নদী}}
\textbf{\bn{নদী}} — \emph{nôdi} — \textquotedblleft{}a river\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নদী}} (\emph{nôdi}) is Sanskrit \emph{nadī}, \textquotedblleft{}river\textquotedblright{}, taken over whole as a learned loan, a tatsama (CDIAL 6943). The word inherited from it is \emph{naï}, which CDIAL lists.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{পুকুর} (pukur)}{পুকুর (pukur)}]{\bn{পুকুর} (pukur) — a pond}

Before the new one: say the Bengali for a forest, then the Bengali for a river.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{পুকুর}}
\textbf{\bn{পুকুর}} — \emph{pukur} — \textquotedblleft{}a pond\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{পুকুর}} (\emph{pukur}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{pauṣkara}, \textquotedblleft{}pertaining to the blue lotus\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8425). It is built on \emph{puṣkara}, \textquotedblleft{}blue lotus\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
